title: Repairing Al7075 surface using cold spray technology with different metal/ceramic powders
InformationInFigures: Yes. Tensile test specimen dimensions, where gauge length is not clear (Fig. 1), Elastic modulus from stress strain curves (Fig. 11)

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Blend_Ratio: Al 44.2 vol. %, Zn 26.7 vol. %, Al2O3 29.1 vol. %
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: sharp-edged and irregularly shaped particles were Al2O3 particles. Zn and Al particles had a round geometry.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: Al2O3 and Ni particles have larger particle sizes compared to Zn and Al powders, facilitating the formation of a structure with reduced voids.
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: Damage was created on the surfaces of Al7075 substrates measuring 200x300x5 mm3 using a ball end mill with a radius of 2.5 mm. A groove with a 1 mm depth was created using a Ø5 mm end mill. Following the milling procedure, the sanding operation was conducted using abrasive Al2O3 particles to achieve a coarser surface roughness

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: The specimens were cut to appropriate dimensions using cutting fluid with a Struers Discotom 5 cutting machine for microstructure examination. Grinding and polishing steps were properly performed for metallographic examination using the Struers TegraPol 21 following standard procedures.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Deposition resembled a lamellar structure (layers), and a dense composite structure. No cracks or voids. Contained 24.8 +/- 4.7 vol. % Al2O3. The powders did not melt, structure was formed through mechanical interlocking and particles retained their properties within the structure. Hard Al2O3 powder increased plastic deformation, decreased likelihood of structural defects, and increased deposition efficiency due to increasing surface roughness of substrate.
